Elena — thank you, and great questions. High level answers up front, followed by next steps and a plan to get a tailored addendum in place.

1) No-training / model-improvement opt-out: yes — Redwood supports a contractual opt-out that prevents customer-provided content (prompts, attachments, responses) from being used to train or improve any models. We typically implement this as an explicit clause in the DPA/Agreement plus a technical flag at ingestion so the data remains segregated. We will propose language you can drop into v4.

2) Ownership: MedTech retains ownership of prompts and outputs you provide/receive. Redwood may collect aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) and limited feature flags for system health; we do not surface or store raw customer content for product-model training when the opt-out is in effect.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: I'll attach our current subprocessor inventory (includes primary cloud, backups, monitoring, SRE partners). Karthik will confirm region-level guarantees and the process for adding/rotating subprocessors. Short answer: our hosted control plane and primary GPUs run in AWS us-west-2 (US), with optional EU-region tenancy for customers who require EU-residency for model execution.

4) Audit evidence: we can share the SOC 2 Type II report and a KMS integration brief. For EU data residency we have a documented data-flow diagram and can provide audit logs on request.

Next steps: Karthik — can you drop proposed contract language for the no-training opt-out and the data-residency clause? We'll also attach the current subprocessor spreadsheet and circle back with a single redline for Elena to review. Prio: get wording that MedTech legal is comfortable with, then DocuSign the addendum.

Elena — attaching: MedTech_DPA_v4.pdf (from your note). I'll attach the subprocessor inventory in my next message.

Hi Elena / team — looping in the privacy/infra details below and attaching the subprocessor inventory. Short answers first, then suggested contract snippets.

- No-training opt-out: operationally enforced. When the opt-out flag is set for an account, all customer content is marked and routed to isolated storage paths and excluded from the model training pipelines. Retention still applies per the DPA; we can shorten retention for MedTech on request (default 30 days logs, configurable).

- Ownership: confirm MedTech retains rights to inputs/outputs. Redwood reserves the right to use aggregated and anonymized telemetry for service improvement; no raw content is used for model training under opt-out.

- Subprocessors: attached spreadsheet includes: AWS (compute & storage) — us-west-2 (primary); GCP (backup snapshots) — europe-west1 (replication disabled unless EU-residency option selected); Sentry (monitoring); Datadog (metrics); Third-party SRE (contracted partner; US). Note: any non-US replication is configurable and disabled by default for customers selecting US-residency. We provide 30 days notice for subprocessor changes and a process for customer objection/escalation.

Suggested DPA snippets you can paste into v4: 

"No-Training Commitment: Redwood Inference will not use, directly or indirectly, Customer Content for purposes of training, fine-tuning, or improving any of Redwood's models or datasets without Customer's prior written consent. Customer Content will be processed and stored in segregated paths when the contractual No-Training Commitment is elected."

"Ownership: Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and any Outputs derived therefrom. Redwood's limited use of aggregate, de-identified telemetry does not affect Customer's ownership rights."

"Subprocessors & Transfers: Redwood's current list of subprocessors is provided in Appendix A. Redwood shall provide notice of any additions or material changes to subprocessors at least thirty (30) days prior to such change and shall permit Customer to reasonably object. For customers requiring EU-only data residency, Redwood will execute region-restricted processing and will not replicate Customer Content outside of the selected region except as required by law."

Attachments: subprocessors_2026-06-08.xlsx (current inventory), plus a short KMS integration brief.

If MedTech wants us to produce a redline, we're happy to prepare one and include the above clauses.

—Karthik
